mainTopic: Milk falling on meat: נותן טעם, whether טעם כעיקר is a Torah law, רב's rule of חתיכה נעשית נבלה, and the debate over אפשר לסוחטו.
overview: The amud opens at the end of an earlier discussion about מראית העין. A question from the סריקין cakes of ביתוס is answered with מר בר רב אשי's words: 'his belt proves it for him.' Then a new משנה teaches that a drop of milk forbids a piece of meat, or a whole stirred pot, only if it gives taste (נותן טעם). אביי says that the rule that taste forbids, even without the actual food, is a Torah law for all איסורים. He proves this from בשר בחלב. רבא rejects the proof: the Torah forbade meat and milk through cooking, so the taste rule there cannot teach us about other איסורים. רב then rules that a piece that absorbed milk becomes נבלה itself and forbids the other pieces, since they are its own kind. רבינא explains that רב's case is thick gravy, so רב does not argue with רבא's view of רבי יהודה. The גמרא shows that רב holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור and lists who holds each side. It then starts a challenge from another ruling of רב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from the Syrian cakes of ביתוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier leniency for one person with the argument the Sages used about סריקין: people will say 'all סריקין are forbidden, yet the סריקין of ביתוס are allowed?' So no individual exception should be made.
steps.simpleTranslation: Will people not say: All the decorated Syrian cakes are forbidden, but the Syrian cakes of ביתוס are allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still in the middle of an earlier discussion about things forbidden because of how they look (מראית העין). It objects to making an exception for one person (washing his only shirt), citing the סריקין case. There the Sages refused ביתוס's request because people would see the exception as inconsistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If something is forbidden only because people might suspect wrongdoing, it should be forbidden for everyone. Allowing one person what everyone else is forbidden looks inconsistent to onlookers. That is why the Sages refused ביתוס, and the same objection seems to apply to the one-shirt leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Decorated Syrian-style cakes, usually forbidden on פסח because they take time to make
Something forbidden only because of how it looks to others
Forbidden / permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the discussion from the previous page. It is not connected to the milk-and-meat משנה that comes right after it.

phrases.english: All the Syrian cakes are forbidden
but the Syrian cakes of Baitos are permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַסְּרִיקִין אֲסוּרִין וּסְרִיקֵי בַיְיתּוֹס מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of מראית העין from the previous page.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that whatever is forbidden because of מראית העין stays forbidden in every situation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some סריקין are permitted, which shows that a prohibition based on appearance can have exceptions.

steps.title: A visible sign removes the suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in that case there is a clear sign that explains things, as מר בר רב אשי said: 'his belt proves it for him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There, as מר בר רב אשי said, his belt is proof for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says that in that case there is a clear sign that shows onlookers nothing wrong is going on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of מראית העין only applies when people might actually suspect wrongdoing. When something visible plainly explains the situation, there is nothing to suspect. A belt worn with the only shirt a person owns is one example. So the exception does not break the rule. It is a case where the reason for the rule is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: His belt
Proves for him, shows clearly what the situation is

steps.whatToRemember: מראית העין does not apply where a clear sign removes any reason for suspicion.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, הָא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: There, Mar bar Rav Ashi already said:
His belt is proof for him.
phrases.notes: People wore one belt over their shirt, so seeing the belt washed with the shirt showed he owned only one shirt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, הָא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a visible sign removes the suspicion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exception seemed to show that מראית העין rules are not absolute.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where a clear sign shows there is nothing wrong, there is no מראית העין to begin with.

steps.title: A drop of milk on a piece of meat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a drop of milk falls on a piece of meat and is enough to give it taste, the piece is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A drop of milk that fell on a piece of meat: if it has enough to give taste to that piece, the piece is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a drop of milk landing on a single piece of meat in a pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is not whether any milk touched the meat. The test is whether the milk is enough to give the meat its taste (נותן טעם). Only then is the piece forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A drop of milk
A piece of meat
Gives taste, enough of the forbidden food to be tasted

phrases.english: MISHNA: A drop of milk
that fell on the piece of meat,
if it has enough to give taste
to that piece, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Milk on a piece of meat forbids that piece only if there is enough milk to give it taste.

steps.title: If the pot was stirred
steps.stepSummary: If the pot was stirred, we measure whether the drop gives taste to the whole pot. If it does, everything is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stirred the pot: if the drop has enough to give taste to that whole pot, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. Here the pot was stirred, so the milk spread through everything in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stirring spreads the drop through the whole pot instead of leaving it in one piece. So we measure the drop against the whole pot. If it can be tasted there, everything is forbidden. If not, everything is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Stirred or shook
Cooking pot

steps.whatToRemember: The measure is always נותן טעם. Only what the milk is measured against changes: the piece, or the whole pot after stirring.

phrases.english: If he stirred the pot,
if it has enough to give taste
to that pot, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After stirring, the drop is measured against the whole pot.

steps.title: אביי: taste counts as the food, by Torah law, for all איסורים
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the principle 'its taste and not its actual substance' (טעם כעיקר) is a Torah law for all forbidden foods, not only for בשר בחלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'Its taste and not its actual substance' is, in general, a Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a rule from אביי. He says that forbidden taste alone makes food forbidden by Torah law, for every איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה showed that milk's taste forbids meat. אביי takes this further. Even when none of the forbidden food itself remains and only its taste does, it is a Torah prohibition, and this applies to all forbidden foods.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Its taste and not its actual substance
In general, for all cases
From the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the famous rule טעם כעיקר דאורייתא, a foundation for the laws of kosher mixtures.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Abaye said:
Its taste and not its actual substance
in general, is from the Torah.
phrases.notes: 'In general' means for all forbidden foods, not just meat and milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טַעְמוֹ וְלֹא מַמָּשׁוֹ בְּעָלְמָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a general Torah rule from the משנה's measure of נותן טעם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טעם כעיקר is a Torah law for all איסורים.

steps.title: Setting up the proof: the only reason not to learn from בשר בחלב
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues: if the rule were only rabbinic, why wouldn't we learn it from בשר בחלב? The only answer would be that בשר בחלב is a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think it is only rabbinic, why don't we learn it from meat and milk? Because that is a חידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts his proof. He imagines the other side's view and states the only reason it could give. This sets up the next step, where that reason will be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בשר בחלב, taste clearly forbids by Torah law. Normally we would extend that to other איסורים. The only way to block this is to say בשר בחלב is a חידוש, an unusual law we cannot copy, since meat and milk are each allowed alone.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would think
Only a rabbinic law
We learn (one law from another)
A novel, unusual law that cannot be copied to other cases

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that it is rabbinic,

phrases.aramaic: מִבָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב מַאי טַעְמָא לָא גָּמְרִינַן?
phrases.english: why don't we learn it from meat and milk?
Because it is a novelty.
phrases.notes: Meat alone and milk alone are both allowed. They are forbidden only together, which makes it an unusual law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for אביי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That טעם כעיקר is a Torah law in general.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah-level rule of taste in בשר בחלב, which could be extended to all איסורים unless it is a חידוש.

steps.title: בשר בחלב is not that kind of חידוש
steps.stepSummary: If בשר בחלב were a true חידוש, it would be forbidden even without a taste. Since it needs נותן טעם, it follows normal rules, and we can learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is a חידוש, it should be forbidden even when there is no giving of taste!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down the 'חידוש' reason. This completes his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real חידוש would not follow normal mixture rules, so even a tiny drop would forbid. But the משנה requires נותן טעם, just like ordinary mixtures. So in this respect בשר בחלב is not a חידוש. We can learn from it that taste forbids by Torah law for all איסורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
There is not

steps.whatToRemember: Because בשר בחלב uses the normal measure of נותן טעם, it is not a חידוש on this point. So טעם כעיקר is דאורייתא for all איסורים.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not say בשר בחלב is not a חידוש at all. It only shows that its taste rule follows normal mixture rules, so we can learn from it.

phrases.english: If it is a novelty,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא נוֹתֵן טַעַם נָמֵי!
phrases.english: then even where there is no giving of taste, too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי חִדּוּשׁ הוּא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא נוֹתֵן טַעַם נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'חידוש' reason offered in step 6, which completes אביי's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that בשר בחלב's taste rule cannot be copied because it is a חידוש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A real חידוש would forbid even without taste, but בשר בחלב requires נותן טעם like ordinary mixtures.

steps.title: רבא: The Torah forbade meat and milk only through cooking
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's proof. בשר בחלב can still be a חידוש. It needs נותן טעם only because the Torah forbade it in the way of cooking, and cooking works through taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: The Torah forbade it in the manner of cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי and knocks down his proof. He says the need for taste in בשר בחלב does not prove it follows normal rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that if בשר בחלב were a חידוש, it would be forbidden even without taste. רבא answers that the איסור itself is defined as 'cooking,' and cooking means the taste passes from one food to the other. So בשר בחלב can still be a חידוש, and we cannot learn טעם כעיקר for other איסורים from it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the manner of cooking: the Torah's איסור of meat and milk is defined by cooking them together
A novel, unusual law that does not follow normal rules, so we cannot learn other cases from it
The Torah forbade

steps.whyThisMatters: Once רבא gives this answer, אביי's source for טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב is gone. רבא's answer does not say that טעם כעיקר is only rabbinic. It only shows that בשר בחלב cannot serve as the source.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is אביי, answering the argument from the last two steps.

phrases.english: The Torah forbade it in the manner of cooking.
phrases.notes: He means it really is a חידוש. Taste matters here only because cooking is how the taste passes over.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: דֶּרֶךְ בִּשּׁוּל אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's reasoning from steps 6-7 that בשר בחלב cannot be a חידוש because it requires נותן טעם.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's whole proof that טעם כעיקר is a Torah law, learned from בשר בחלב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי assumed that needing taste means בשר בחלב is not a חידוש. In fact, the taste requirement comes from how the איסור is defined (cooking), so it can still be a חידוש.

steps.title: רב: The flavored piece itself becomes forbidden meat
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that once milk gives taste to a piece of meat, that piece itself becomes נבלה. It then forbids all the other pieces in the pot because they are the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Once it gave taste to the piece, the piece itself becomes נבלה, and it forbids all the pieces, because they are its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a drop of milk falling on a piece of meat. It brings רב's ruling on what happens to the other pieces in the pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says the absorbed piece does not just contain some forbidden milk. The piece itself turns into a forbidden item, like נבלה. Since the other pieces are also meat, the same kind, they cannot nullify it, so the whole pot becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The piece itself becomes like נבלה: the whole piece now counts as a forbidden food in its own right
Literally a non-kosher carcass. Here it means a piece that is fully forbidden
Its own kind: the same type of food (meat with meat)
Once, since

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think only the bit of milk inside the piece is forbidden. רב says the entire piece becomes forbidden. That is why it can forbid everything else.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the famous idea of חתיכה נעשית נבלה, which shapes many later rulings about כשרות.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתַן טַעַם בַּחֲתִיכָה,
phrases.english: Rav said: Once it gave taste to the piece,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the drop of milk from the משנה.

phrases.english: the piece itself becomes forbidden meat (נבלה),
and it forbids all the pieces, every one of them,
because they are its own kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתַן טַעַם בַּחֲתִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, returning to the משנה's case from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A piece that has absorbed the taste of milk becomes a forbidden item itself. It forbids all the other pieces of meat, since a food mixed with its own kind is not nullified.

steps.title: Does רב follow רבי יהודה and disagree with רבא?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא notes that רב's reason ('they are its own kind') matches רבי יהודה's view that מין במינו לא בטיל. He asks whether רב then disagrees with רבא's explanation of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי said to רבינא: Now, whose view did רב follow in his ruling? רבי יהודה's, who said that a kind mixed with its own kind is not nullified. Shall we say רב disagrees with רבא?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא raises a problem with רב's ruling. He first identifies whose opinion רב follows, then suggests that רב argues with רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason 'because they are its own kind' only works for someone who holds that a food mixed with its own kind is never nullified, and that is רבי יהודה. But רבא understood רבי יהודה in a more limited way, which is explained in the next step. So it seems רב and רבא disagree about רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A food mixed with its own kind is not nullified (רבי יהודה's view)
Now consider: an opening that sets up a logical point
In line with whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
Shall we say he disagrees? This suggests a conflict between two אמוראים

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari said to Ravina:
Now, in line with whom did Rav say his ruling?

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר מִין בְּמִינוֹ לֹא בָּטֵיל,
phrases.english: In line with Rabbi Yehuda, who said a kind mixed with its own kind is not nullified,
shall we say he disagrees with Rava?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 9 by linking it to רבי יהודה and setting it against רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the forbidden piece forbids all the pieces because they are its own kind.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב must follow רבי יהודה. But רבא's version of רבי יהודה would not reach רב's result, so רב seems to argue with רבא.

steps.title: רבא's explanation of רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבא's statement. In a mixture of a forbidden food, the same kind, and a different kind, we ignore the same kind. If the different kind is more than the forbidden food, it nullifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: רבי יהודה holds that whenever there is a kind, its own kind, and something else, remove its own kind as if it is not there, and what is not its kind outweighs it and nullifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's statement to show why רב seems to disagree with him. This completes the challenge from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, even רבי יהודה lets a different kind nullify the forbidden food if there is enough of it. The same-kind food is simply set aside. In רב's pot there is also gravy, which is a different kind, so by רבא's rule it should nullify the forbidden piece. רב did not say that, so he seems to disagree with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion
Remove its own kind as if it were not there: ignore the same-kind food when measuring
What is not its kind: the different type of food in the mixture
Is more than it and nullifies it

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say that רבי יהודה lets the same kind nullify. The same kind is still ignored. Only the different kind can do the nullifying.

phrases.english: As Rava said: Rabbi Yehuda holds,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא מִין וּמִינוֹ וְדָבָר אַחֵר –
phrases.english: whenever there is a forbidden kind, its own kind, and something else,
phrases.notes: Picture three things together: the forbidden food, permitted food of the same type, and a permitted food of a different type.

phrases.english: remove its own kind as if it is not there,
and what is not its kind outweighs it and nullifies it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the 'disagrees with רבא' challenge in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רב disagrees with רבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's statement that, according to רבי יהודה, the same kind is ignored and a larger amount of a different kind nullifies the forbidden food.

steps.title: רב was talking about thick gravy
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers מר זוטרא. In thin gravy, רב would agree the piece is nullified. רב's case is thick gravy, which is the same kind as the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it fell into thin gravy, you are right. But here we are dealing with a case where it fell into thick gravy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers מר זוטרא's question. רב does not argue with רבא, because רב's case is about thick gravy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that a different kind which outnumbers the forbidden food nullifies it. Thin gravy would count as a different kind, so the piece would be nullified, and רב would agree. Thick gravy is full of meat, so everything in the pot is the same kind, and nothing different is there to nullify the piece.

keyTerms.meaning: Thin, watery gravy
Thick gravy, full of meat
What case are we dealing with here? This phrase introduces a narrower case
So it is indeed; I agree

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבינא answering מר זוטרא's question from before.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דִּנְפַל בְּרוֹטֶב רַכָּה – הָכִי נָמֵי,
phrases.english: If it fell into thin gravy, so it is indeed;
Here, what are we dealing with?
Where it fell into thick gravy.
phrases.notes: Thick gravy is full of meat, so it counts as the same kind as the meat pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Steps 10-11 about whether רב disagrees with רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): רב's ruling applies only to thick gravy.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to say the same kind forbids the pot even when a different kind (the gravy) is present, which would go against רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's case has only the same kind (thick gravy), so he agrees with רבא's rule.

steps.title: Why would the piece itself become forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב's view is. If he held that squeezable taste is permitted, why would the piece become נבלה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רב hold? If he holds that something that can be squeezed out is permitted, why does the piece become נבלה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's main ruling and asks what idea is behind it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The milk inside the piece could in theory be squeezed out and spread through the pot. If that is enough to keep the piece permitted, the milk should just mix into the pot and be nullified. So why call the piece itself נבלה?

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; his view is
It is possible to squeeze it out: the forbidden taste could be pressed out of the food
Why?
Forbidden like a non-kosher carcass; here it means the piece itself is now a forbidden item

phrases.english: And what does he hold?
phrases.notes: "He" is רב, from his ruling in Step 9.

phrases.english: If he holds that something that can be squeezed out is permitted,
why does the piece become נבלה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gravy question and asks about the reasoning behind רב's original ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which view on אפשר לסוחטו רב's ruling depends on.

steps.title: רב holds that squeezable taste is still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב must hold אפשר לסוחטו אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he holds that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. רב must hold that the piece stays forbidden even though the milk could be squeezed out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the piece absorbs the forbidden taste, the piece itself is treated as forbidden. The chance of squeezing the milk out does not help. That is why it becomes נבלה and can forbid the other pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces the correct option after the first one was rejected
Forbidden
Even if the taste could be squeezed out, the food stays forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רב's idea that "the piece itself becomes נבלה" depends on holding אפשר לסוחטו אסור.

phrases.english: Rather, he holds that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden.

steps.title: Who holds each view on squeezing
steps.stepSummary: A source records the disagreement: רב, רבי חנינא and רבי יוחנן say forbidden; שמואל, רבי שמעון בר רבי and ריש לקיש say permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: רב, רבי חנינא and רבי יוחנן say that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden. שמואל, רבי שמעון son of רבי, and ריש לקיש say that something that can be squeezed out is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last step with a known source. רב is listed among those who say אפשר לסוחטו אסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the view the גמרא gave רב really is his recorded position. It also shows that this is a known disagreement, with three אמוראים on each side.

keyTerms.meaning: If the taste could be squeezed out, the food is permitted
Permitted
Who say (plural); a group sharing one view

phrases.english: As it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַב וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rav, Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yochanan, who say:
Something that can be squeezed out is forbidden;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּאֵל וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Shmuel, Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi, and Reish Lakish, who say:
Something that can be squeezed out is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 14 by citing רב's recorded view.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An איתמר listing the two groups of אמוראים in the disagreement.

steps.title: Challenge from רב's ruling on meat in a pot of milk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רב really holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור. It quotes his ruling that an olive-sized piece of meat in a pot of milk is forbidden while the milk is permitted. The question is still being built and is completed on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רב hold that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden? But it was stated: An olive-sized piece of meat that fell into a pot of milk, רב said: The meat is forbidden and the milk is permitted. And if you think that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against Step 14 by quoting another ruling of רב. The sentence is not finished yet; the next part of the גמרא completes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ruling, the meat absorbed milk and became forbidden, but the milk stays permitted. The גמרא is about to show that if the meat itself counted as forbidden (אפשר לסוחטו אסור), this ruling would not fit. So רב's two rulings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's size; a basic halachic measure
A large cooking pot
The meat is forbidden and the milk is permitted
And if you think that...; sets up a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at "the meat is forbidden and the milk is permitted" and think the question is done. The real contradiction comes in the next part, after "ואי סלקא דעתך".

phrases.english: And does Rav hold that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden?
But wasn't it stated:

phrases.aramaic: כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ יוֹרָה שֶׁל חָלָב,
phrases.english: An olive-sized piece of meat that fell into a pot of milk,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: בָּשָׂר אָסוּר וְחָלָב מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: Rav said: The meat is forbidden and the milk is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ אָסוּר,
phrases.english: And if you think that something that can be squeezed out is forbidden,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַב אֶפְשָׁר לְסוֹחֳטוֹ אָסוּר? וְהָאִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view given to רב in Steps 14-15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב holds אפשר לסוחטו אסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ruling of רב (meat forbidden, milk permitted) seems not to fit the idea that the meat itself becomes forbidden. The full argument continues after "ואי סלקא דעתך".
